findings.title: A failed mermaid chunk load is cached, so every later README fails until the page is reloaded.
findings.body: `loadMermaid` stores the `import('mermaid')` promise in a module-level variable and never clears it. If the chunk fails to load once (a network blip or a deploy that changes chunk hashes), `mermaidPromise` stays rejected. Every later call to `renderMermaidDiagrams`, including after a theme switch or when opening another folder, then goes straight to the catch block and marks all diagrams as failed, with no retry until a full page reload. Fix: reset the cache when the import fails, e.g. `mermaidPromise = import('mermaid').then(m => m.default).catch(e => { mermaidPromise = undefined; throw e; });`.

held.title: The new resolution forces mermaid onto an older version of its URL sanitizer.
held.body: `"mermaid/@braintree/sanitize-url": "7.0.1"` pins the URL sanitizer that mermaid uses for link and `click` hrefs to 7.0.1. Recent mermaid 11.x declares a higher `^7.1.x` range for this package, so the override likely goes below what mermaid expects. The PR gives no reason for it. This is the library that cleans attacker-controlled URLs in untrusted README diagrams, so running mermaid against an older or API-incompatible version could weaken that cleaning or break rendering. I could not check mermaid 11.16.0's declared range or whether 7.0.1 lacks fixes mermaid depends on. Remove the override, or document why it is safe and matches mermaid's declared range.
